title: Passwords & 2FA
examples: What makes a password really strong?
Should I write my passwords down somewhere?
What is the difference between a password and a passphrase?

explain.say: A strong password is long and mixes different types of characters.
A passphrase is much easier to remember than a random string of characters.
Never use personal information like your pet's name or birthday in a password.
Password managers are safe programs that store all your complex passwords for you.
Two-Factor Authentication adds a second layer of security beyond just your password.
In real life, think about securing your online accounts like securing your house.

faq.q: Why do I need a password manager?
faq.a: A password manager keeps all your unique and complex passwords safe in one encrypted place. It means you only have to remember one very strong master password.
asks: Where can I store all my passwords safely?
Is it okay to use a password manager?

faq.q: What is the best thing to use for a password?
faq.a: The best passwords are long passphrases that mix random words and symbols. They should not contain any information about you.
asks: Should I use a sentence as a password?

faq.q: What does two-factor authentication actually do?
faq.a: It requires two different types of proof to log in, like something you know and something you have. This stops someone from getting in even if they steal your password.
asks: Do I always need two factors?

faq.q: Can I use the same password for everything?
faq.a: No, you should never reuse passwords across different accounts. If one site gets hacked, all your accounts would be at risk.
asks: Is it safe to use one password?
Should I change my password often?

faq.q: How long should my password be?
faq.a: Security experts recommend passwords that are at least twelve characters long. Length is often more important than complexity alone.

facts: Passwords should be unique for every important account.
A passphrase is a sequence of random words, making it very strong.
Two-Factor Authentication requires two different verification methods.
Password managers encrypt and store your credentials securely.

quiz.say: Which of these is the strongest password?
quiz.why: This option is strong because it is long and mixes uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols.

wrong.1: This is too short and only uses letters and numbers.
wrong.2: This is a passphrase but lacks symbols and numbers for extra strength.
wrong.3: This is a very common pattern that hackers guess easily.

quiz.say: If you use a password manager, what is the most important thing to remember?
quiz.why: The master password unlocks the entire vault, so keeping it secret is vital.

wrong.1: This is often used for recovery but is not the master key.
wrong.2: Security questions can often be guessed or found through social media.
wrong.3: This is used for 2FA, not for unlocking the manager itself.

options.show: Being physically present at the site
options.say: Being physically present at the site

quiz.why: It proves you have something physical, like your phone, in addition to knowing the password.

wrong.0: This is just another password, not a second factor.
wrong.1: While this is a factor, 2FA usually refers to a code sent via a separate method.
wrong.2: This is a physical check, not the standard digital second factor.
